subject: Edge isolation and data residency — deployment constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@cardiussec.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@cardiussec.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Edge isolation and data residency — deployment constraints & next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and items we promised to follow up on. I tried to capture the constraints you emphasized so we can make sure SRE/security are aligned before the technical deep dive.

Key pain points and drivers (as discussed):
- Regulatory: equivalent to FedRAMP controls for third-party inference; strict data residency (US-east) for patient-related telemetry.
- Isolation: certain workloads must be air-gapped or run in a fully isolated VPC with no general internet egress.
- Key management: customer-managed KMS/HSM required; no vendor-held root keys.
- Auditability: full audit logs, token-level traceability, and retention for 7 years for a subset of logs.

High-level hosting options we outlined:
1) Private VPC (preferred path): Redwood Private deployed into a customer VPC (no public egress; allow only a small set of outbound IPs / endpoints for model updates) + customer KMS.
2) Air-gapped on-prem appliance model: isolated inference nodes with offline model delivery and signed manifests.

Open questions we promised to clarify:
- Exact list of allowed outbound IPs and whether AWS-native services (CloudWatch, CloudHSM) are acceptable.
- Frequency/expectations for model updates if you choose offline sync.
- Any contractual language requirements for data retention and auditability.

Actions / next steps / owners:
- Kimberly: send consolidated network requirements and the SOW template (attached).
- Cardius: share current network diagram and list of egress restrictions (Priya) — aiming for that before the deep dive.
- Redwood Solutions: schedule infra deep-dive (proposed window in my calendar below).

Attachments: cardius_network_requirements_v2.pdf (network checklist), SOW-template.docx (contract skeleton).

Proposed deep-dive: Thu, Oct 8, 10:00–11:30 PT — please confirm if that works; we can expand to include Marcus Lin (solutions engineer) and our Security lead.

Thanks — Kim

From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@cardiussec.com>

Subject: Re: Edge isolation and data residency — deployment constraints & next steps

Kimberly — thanks for the recap; this matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Regulatory context: we are working under an internal equivalency program (not formally FedRAMP but comparable controls for customer data). Any solution will need to demonstrate separation of duties, key custody options (CloudHSM is acceptable for AWS-hosted KMS) and cryptographic attestations for model bundles.

2) Networking: our current setup is hybrid — on-prem VMware clusters plus AWS us-east-1. For the VPC path we can permit outbound connections to a short allowlist of IPs and FQDNs (we'll generate that list). Public internet egress is not allowed; all endpoints must be TLS mutual-auth where possible.

3) Data & retention: audit logs for inference requests must be retained for 7 years for regulated customers; we also need capability to export logs to our SIEM (Splunk).

4) On air-gap: air-gapped on-prem is the preference for a pilot. We need to understand the mechanics for model updates — ideally a signed bundle delivered via SFTP or shipped media, with integrity checks.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports:
- Model bundles with signed checksums for offline install?
- A fully offline inference runtime (no control-plane egress) with local telemetry that can be exported at rest?

Oct 8 works for a deep-dive team call; Priya and I will prepare our network diagram and a short list of IDs/IPs.

— Alex
Alex Monroe | Head of Infrastructure, Cardius Security

Alex / Priya — looping back with the promised artifacts and a succinct set of next steps so everyone has clarity before Thursday's deep-dive.

What we heard (short):
- Regulatory need for FedRAMP-like controls, US-East residency for regulated datasets.
- No general internet egress from the inference plane; allowlist-only outbound for model sync and telemetry.
- Customer-managed keys (CloudHSM acceptable) and signed model bundles for offline installs.
- 7-year retention requirement for selected audit logs and ability to export to Splunk.

What Redwood can offer (initial options):
- Private VPC deployment into Cardius account with strict allowlist and mTLS endpoints; Redwood control-plane access can be limited to specific egress ranges and mutual-auth endpoints.
- Air-gapped on-prem pilot: signed model bundles + offline runtime; model updates via SFTP or physical media and integrity verification at install.

Immediate next steps (owners & timeline):
1) Cardius (Priya) — send network diagram + allowlist + any existing SOC/audit docs by EOD Wed, Oct 7.
2) Redwood (Ben & Marcus) — produce two short proposal sketches (Private VPC vs Air-gap) and a ballpark price for pilot by Fri, Oct 9.
3) All — technical deep-dive Thu, Oct 8, 10:00–11:30 PT (calendar invite sent).

Attachments: cardius_network_requirements_v2.pdf, SOW-template.docx (Ben updated placeholders for both options).

If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag now and we'll adjust prior to the call. Looking forward — Kim
